From e4dd748dc87cf431af7b3954963be0d9f6150217 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2022 13:44:21 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: fsl_sai: Fix FSL_SAI_xDR/xFR definition

There are multiple xDR and xFR registers, the index is
from 0 to 7. FSL_SAI_xDR and FSL_SAI_xFR is abandoned,
replace them with FSL_SAI_xDR0 and FSL_SAI_xFR0.

Fixes: 4f7a0728b530 ("ASoC: fsl_sai: Add support for SAI new version")
Signed-off-by: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1653284661-18964-1-git-send-email-shengjiu.wang@nxp.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h b/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
index e4965efe6102..1c8f5ca07f9d 100644
--- a/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
+++ b/sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h
@@ -80,8 +80,8 @@
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR3(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR3(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR3(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR4(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR4(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR4(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR5(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR5(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR5(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xDR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RDR(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xFR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RFR(ofs))
+#define FSL_SAI_xDR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR0 : FSL_SAI_RDR0)
+#define FSL_SAI_xFR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR0 : FSL_SAI_RFR0)
 #define FSL_SAI_xMR(tx)		(tx ? FSL_SAI_TMR : FSL_SAI_RMR)
 
 /* SAI Transmit/Receive Control Register */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `sound/soc/fsl/fsl_sai.h`**
   - The definitions for `FSL_SAI_xDR` and `FSL_SAI_xFR` have been removed.
   - These have been replaced with `FSL_SAI_xDR0` and `FSL_SAI_xFR0`, which are now defined to reference the specific transmit and receive data registers (TDR0 and RDR0, TFR0 and RFR0) for index 0.

### Relationships
- The changes made in `fsl_sai.h` are intended to correct the handling of multiple xDR and xFR registers by specifying the index explicitly (using 0). This modification addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the fix reference) that did not account for the multiple instances of these registers, thereby improving the clarity and correctness of the register definitions in the code.

Here is the commit message:
ASoC: fsl_sai: Fix FSL_SAI_xDR/xFR definition

There are multiple xDR and xFR registers, the index is
from 0 to 7. FSL_SAI_xDR and FSL_SAI_xFR is abandoned,
replace them with FSL_SAI_xDR0 and FSL_SAI_xFR0.

Fixes: 4f7a0728b530 ("ASoC: fsl_sai: Add support for SAI new version")
Signed-off-by: Shengjiu Wang <shengjiu.wang@nxp.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1653284661-18964-1-git-send-email-shengjiu.wang@nxp.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the use of generic definitions for `FSL_SAI_xDR` and `FSL_SAI_xFR`, which did not specify the register index, leading to ambiguity and potential conflicts when multiple xDR and xFR registers (indexed from 0 to 7) exist. This oversight resulted in incorrect register references in the code, particularly for the new version of the SAI that introduced these multiple registers.

Here is the patch:
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR4(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR4(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR4(ofs))
 #define FSL_SAI_xCR5(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TCR5(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RCR5(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xDR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RDR(ofs))
-#define FSL_SAI_xFR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RFR(ofs))
+#define FSL_SAI_xDR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR0 : FSL_SAI_RDR0)
+#define FSL_SAI_xFR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR0 : FSL_SAI_RFR0)
 #define FSL_SAI_xMR(tx)		(tx ? FSL_SAI_TMR : FSL_SAI_RMR)

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define FSL_SAI_xDR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RDR(ofs))
#define FSL_SAI_xFR(tx, ofs)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR(ofs) : FSL_SAI_RFR(ofs))
```
Reason:
The use of generic definitions for `FSL_SAI_xDR` and `FSL_SAI_xFR` without specifying the register index leads to ambiguity when multiple xDR and xFR registers exist (indexed from 0 to 7). This can cause incorrect register references, particularly in the context of the new SAI version that introduced these multiple registers.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define FSL_SAI_xDR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TDR0 : FSL_SAI_RDR0)
#define FSL_SAI_xFR0(tx)	(tx ? FSL_SAI_TFR0 : FSL_SAI_RFR0)
```
Reason:
The patch replaces the ambiguous generic definitions with specific definitions for `FSL_SAI_xDR0` and `FSL_SAI_xFR0`, which clearly reference the correct registers (TDR0 and RDR0, TFR0 and RFR0). This eliminates the ambiguity and potential conflicts, ensuring that the correct registers are accessed in the code.
